ratings.why: The request says a ticket must match every filter given, and this 200 response still returns Dana Lee's ticket when the query also requires Kim, so an operator silently gets the wrong queue.
The notice does reach the relay file the operator already tails, but `to` is only the bare agent name while every existing notice is an email and nothing says how to resolve that name to a mailbox.
The CLI prints the README's unassigned mark for the stored name "—", so an operator will treat an assigned ticket as unassigned.

U+2028, U+2029 and U+0085 are accepted and a standard line split turns one raw ticket row into two, but they are rare and outside the control-character check the service already uses for single-line fields.
An unpaired surrogate is not a name an operator will assign; the request only requires a non-empty name of at most 64 characters, so rejecting ill-formed UTF-16 is extra hardening.
